clusters.name: After grandfather's death, 1989–1990
clusters.reason: Around the time your grandfather died in July 1989, your mother was lying awake over money and stopped talking with your father about it. Within a few months, your brother's grades fell. Your mother calmed down once back at work in early 1990. The pile of shifts in your parents' distance, your brother's functioning, and your mother's anxiety around your grandfather's death marks a period of heightened difficulty.

clusters.name: After mother's cancer diagnosis, 1994–1996
clusters.reason: You left for college in September 1993. Within months you developed migraines and called your brother most nights. Your mother was diagnosed with breast cancer in early 1995. Around that time you stopped returning your brother's calls, and within a year you stopped calling home. Your symptoms, the shifts in your relationships with your brother and mother, and your mother's serious diagnosis all clustered in this span as the family faced her illness.
clusters.change: The run began with your leaving for college, but the diagnosis of your mother's cancer in early 1995 is the change that opened this period of heightened difficulty.
